# Case `R04_loader`

**Category:** reclaim-method (How the pile was taken back)
**Source:** synthetic · **Split:** holdout

## Why it is in the matrix

Scattered front-end loader bites from the top of a few accessible columns. Fewest layers, least spatial averaging, and the real run-of-mine pad case rather than the blending-bed ideal.

## Expected behaviour

The worst VRR of the reclaim axis, plausibly close to 1 (little or no blending)

## Kill criterion

> If VRR(R04) is the best of the reclaim axis the cell selection is wrong

This is the statement that turns the case from a demonstration into a test. It says, in advance, what
result would mean the code is wrong, and the release gate fails the bake when it is violated.

## Configuration

| parameter | value | what it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `stacking` | `chevron` | the deposition path over the pad |
| `reclaim` | `loader` | which cells the machine engages and how deep it reaches |
| `n_passes` | 24 | stacker passes, that is layers: the N of the 1/N bound |
| `sr` | 1.0 | the Gray-Thornton segregation number; 0 is a passive tracer |
| `repose_deg` | 37.0 | the imposed angle of repose of the fine species |
| `repose_coarse_deg` | 37.0 | the coarse species; a positive difference is Makse |
| `structure` | `stationary` | the autocorrelation structure of the incoming stream |
| `range_t` | 4000 t | the practical range of the input variogram, in tonnes |
| `n_dumps` | 320 | truck loads in the build |
| `reclaim_rate` | 1.0 | tonnes reclaimed per tonne stacked |
| `cut_tonnes` | 900 t | the parcel size the plant receives |
| pad | 64 x 24 cells at 3.0 m | 192 by 72 metres |

## Operating regimes

The family sweeps `cut_tonnes`, the parameter this case's category actually turns on. Selecting
a regime in the app re-runs the engine in the browser rather than loading a pre-baked frame,
so the sweep is continuous with the rail's own controls.

| regime | `cut_tonnes` | what it shows |
|---|---|---|
| 300 t | `300.0` | A small parcel. The reclaim geometry shows through most clearly here, because a small cut cannot integrate over enough of the face to hide it. |
| 600 t | `600.0` | A short fleet cycle: roughly three truck loads to the plant at a time. Still small enough that a shallow-reaching machine has to walk to fill it. |
| 900 t | `900.0` | The reference parcel, and the default of the other axes. |
| 1200 t | `1200.0` | A larger draw. More of the face per cut, so the machines start to look alike. |
| 1800 t | `1800.0` | A shift-scale parcel. The reclaim axis is now mostly averaged away. |
| 2400 t | `2400.0` | Large enough that the cut spans several stations, which is a different machine duty from the one the geometry describes; read the layer count rather than the ratio here. |

## Reproduce it

```bash
python data-pipeline/run.py R04_loader --output build/check --band-seeds 5
```

Omit `--output` only for an intentional canonical release bake. Everything about this case is a pure
function of its parameters and the seed, so two runs produce a byte-identical trace.
